content.body:
The British Rifle Grenadier is unique in that he is armed with the only anti-tank grenade in Battleground Europe. The No.36 Mills bomb was fired from a cup fitted to the end of a regular Lee-Enfield rifle employing a special high charge "blank" cartridge loaded into the breech.
While effective against tanks or armored vehicles, it did lose that effectiveness as armor became thicker later in the war, requiring the rifleman to gain an almost ideal, perfect angle shot at 90 degree obliquity to the target, very difficult under most combat circumstances. For these reasons, generally only the very skilled and careful rifle grenadiers do well against most tanks, and the HEAT properties of this grenade are not well suited against enemy infantry.
content.brief: WEAPON: Lee-Enfield No.4 Mk I Rifle AMMO: .303 cal (7.7 mm) British Mk.VII Ball MAGAZINE: 10 rounds (two stripper clips) MUZZLE VELOCITY: 751 m/s RATE OF FIRE: Single-round bolt action OTHER EQUIPMENT: Detachable grenade cup Rifle-fired HE grenades (8) No.36 Mills Bomb HE Grenades (4) No.77 Mk I Smoke Grenades (4) Combat Knife
